title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is experiencing a mix of strategic partnerships and funding rounds, with a notable focus on resilience and data capabilities. Meanwhile, the military's interest in commercial space and AI continues to reshape traditional defense frameworks.

themes.title: Funding Rounds Galore
themes.body: True Anomaly's $190M Series C and Impulse Space's $500M Series D highlight a robust appetite for investment in space tech. These rounds suggest investors are betting on the future of orbital data and tactical capabilities.

themes.title: Military Meets Commercial Space
themes.body: The NRO's acknowledgment of commercial space and AI's impact on spy satellites signals a shift in how defense agencies view their operational frameworks. Partnerships like Anduril and L3Harris's tactical SDA constellation bid further blur the lines between private and public sector capabilities.

themes.title: European Space Defense Gaps
themes.body: While Europe is rearming in various sectors, its space capabilities seem to be lagging. This could create vulnerabilities as geopolitical tensions rise and reliance on space assets becomes more critical.

themes.title: Launch Delays and Design Reviews
themes.body: Blue Origin's New Glenn launch timeline is once again in question, and Sierra Space's Dream Chaser has just cleared a critical design review. These developments underscore the ongoing challenges and milestones in the race to operationalize new space vehicles.
